theory.intro: In an **annuity due**, payments are made at the **beginning** of each period. Because every deposit is invested for one additional compounding period, each payment earns an extra factor of $(1+r)$ compared to an ordinary annuity.
facts: The first deposit compounds for $n$ full periods to $a(1+r)^{n}$, while the final deposit compounds for $1$ period to $a(1+r)$.
Factoring out $a(1+r)$ gives a geometric series with first term $a(1+r)$ and common ratio $1+r$.
The future value formula for an annuity due is $FV = a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$.
An annuity due always accumulates more interest than an ordinary annuity with identical payments and rates.
steps: Identify $a$, the interest rate per period $r$, and the number of periods $n$.
Write the series of terms starting from $a(1+r)$ up to $a(1+r)^{n}$.
Sum the geometric series using $FV = a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ and evaluate.

foundation.question_text: A deposit of $\$1000$ is made at the beginning of each year for $5\text{ years}$ into an account earning $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Write the future value as a geometric series and calculate the balance at the end of $5\text{ years}$.
Show that for $n$ start-of-year deposits of $\$a$ at interest rate $r$ per annum, the future value is $FV = a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Write the series of terms starting from $a(1+r)$ up to $a(1+r)^{n}$.**
First deposit grows for $n$ years: $a(1+r)^{n}$
Last deposit grows for $1$ year: $a(1+r)$
$FV = a(1+r) + a(1+r)^{2} + \dots + a(1+r)^{n}$
2. **Sum the geometric series using $FV = a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ and evaluate.**
First term is $a(1+r)$, common ratio is $1+r$, number of terms is $n$
$FV = \dfrac{a(1+r)((1+r)^{n}-1)}{(1+r)-1}$
$= a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$

foundation.question_text: A parent deposits $\$2000$ at the beginning of each year for $8\text{ years}$ into a college fund earning $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Find the future value of the annuity due.

James contributes $\$300$ at the beginning of each month for $4\text{ years}$ into a savings plan paying $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Calculate the value of the investment at the end of the $4\text{ years}$.

Sophia needs $\$12\,000$ in $3\text{ years}$ for a vehicle purchase. She will make deposits at the beginning of each month into an account paying $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Find the required monthly deposit.

Compare depositing $\$1500$ at the beginning of each year versus at the end of each year for $10\text{ years}$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Find the additional amount accumulated by making start-of-year deposits.
An organization invests $\$5000$ at the beginning of each year for $6\text{ years}$ into a charity reserve earning $8\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Calculate the future value.

development.question_text: On each birthday starting on her 1st birthday up to and including her 18th birthday ($18\text{ deposits}$), Chloe's parents deposit $\$400$ into an investment earning $6.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Calculate the total in the account on her 18th birthday immediately after the 18th deposit interest period.
development.solution_text:
Since deposits are made on each birthday, the first deposit earns 18 years of interest and the 18th deposit earns 1 year of interest.
$a = 400$, $r = 0.065$, $n = 18$
$FV = \dfrac{400(1.065)(1.065^{18}-1)}{0.065}$
$= \$13\,890.35$

development.question_text: A tenant deposits $\$650$ at the beginning of each quarter into a sinking fund earning $5.6\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly for $7\text{ years}$. Calculate the final balance of the fund.

A club wants to have $\$45\,000$ in $5\text{ years}$ to renovate its clubhouse. The committee plans to make equal contributions at the beginning of each month into an account earning $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Calculate the required monthly contribution.

An investor deposits $\$800$ at the beginning of each month for $10\text{ years}$ at $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Calculate how much more interest is earned compared to making the same deposits at the end of each month.

A small business invests $\$1200$ at the beginning of every $6\text{ months}$ for $8\text{ years}$ into a capital reserve fund earning $6.2\%$ p.a. compounded half-yearly. Find the future value of the reserve fund.
A family sets a target of saving $\$60\,000$ in $6\text{ years}$ with equal start-of-year deposits earning $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Find the required annual deposit.

Write out the first three and last two terms of the geometric series for an annuity due with monthly payments of $\$250$ at $4.8\%$ p.a. compounded monthly over $5\text{ years}$ ($n=60$), and evaluate the total future value.

mastery.question_text: A company contributes $\$10\,000$ on 1st January each year ($n=20\text{ contributions}$) into a retirement scheme earning $8.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually. (a) Calculate the total value at the end of the 20th year. (b) Calculate the annual contribution $M$ required for the fund to reach exactly $\$1\,000\,000$ at the end of the 20th year.

An investor deposits $\$500$ at the start of each month into an annuity earning $6.6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly for $15\text{ years}$. Determine the exact dollar difference in the total interest earned between making deposits at the start of each month versus making the same deposits at the end of each month.

A scholarship fund receives $\$3000$ on 1st January every year for $12\text{ years}$ at $7\%$ p.a. compounded annually. Show by geometric series derivation why the future value is $FV = \dfrac{3000 \times 1.07 \times (1.07^{12}-1)}{0.07}$ and evaluate the exact difference in value between the very first deposit and the final deposit on the maturity date.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Write the series of terms starting from $a(1+r)$ up to $a(1+r)^{n}$.**
First deposit made at start of year 1 compounds for 12 years: $3000(1.07)^{12}$
Final deposit made at start of year 12 compounds for 1 year: $3000(1.07)$
$FV = 3000(1.07) + 3000(1.07)^{2} + \dots + 3000(1.07)^{12}$
2. **Sum the geometric series using $FV = a(1+r)\left[\dfrac{(1+r)^{n}-1}{r}\right]$ and evaluate.**
$= \dfrac{3000(1.07)(1.07^{12}-1)}{0.07} = \$57\,376.12$
Value of first deposit $= 3000(1.07)^{12} = \$6755.75$
Value of final deposit $= 3000(1.07) = \$3210.00$
$\text{Difference} = 6755.75 - 3210.00$
$= \$3545.75$
